builder_plan.scenario: A multi-step product task fails because the agent loses track of dependencies.
builder_plan.change: Try the proposed planning step on tasks with checkable intermediate outcomes.
builder_plan.baseline: The same agent solving the same tasks without the new planning step.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task completion, unnecessary steps, planning tokens, response time, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Binary Discrete Diffusion: Candidate-Set Diffusion for Logic and Planning Tasks
summary: It replaces masked and uniform discrete-diffusion corruption kernels with a candidate-set state (a binary membership vector per position) that changes through gradual additions and removals, explicitly representing partial uncertainty during iterative generation. It costs a new training and sampling stack rather than an off-the-shelf API model, since the reader would need to train or fine-tune task-specific diffusion models on a single 24 GB GPU, and adds kernel and sampler complexity relative to standard masked diffusion. It can fail because the demonstrated wins are confined to small structured logic and planning benchmarks at modest scale, gains may not transfer to general LLM reasoning or coding workloads, and per-position set representations raise memory and compute per step compared with single-token states.
rationale: The quality claim is credible but demonstrated only on small structured tasks with custom-trained models, so it merits a small-scale validation experiment rather than production adoption for an API-and-single-GPU team.
technique: Candidate-set binary discrete diffusion for reasoning

claims.statement: It replaces masked and uniform discrete-diffusion corruption kernels with a candidate-set state (a binary membership vector per position) that changes through gradual additions and removals, explicitly representing partial uncertainty during iterative generation. It costs a new training and sampling stack rather than an off-the-shelf API model, since the reader would need to train or fine-tune task-specific diffusion models on a single 24 GB GPU, and adds kernel and sampler complexity relative to standard masked diffusion. It can fail because the demonstrated wins are confined to small structured logic and planning benchmarks at modest scale, gains may not transfer to general LLM reasoning or coding workloads, and per-position set representations raise memory and compute per step compared with single-token states.

Symmetric binary diffusion consistently outperforms tuned masked and uniform discrete-diffusion baselines on Sudoku-Extreme, Boxoban, and graph coloring under matched architectures and budgets, with the largest gains on the hardest instances, while remaining competitive on Text8, TinyStories, and OpenWebText language modeling.
